text:
Alex (AE): Heads-up — GovCo asked for an air-gapped POC. They specifically called out a 'phased bootstrapping' approach and want us to validate sideload testing + upgrade cadence in a 2-week POC. Can we map what we can commit to?
Marta (SE): We can do a two-phase plan:
  1) Seed install (operator + runtime image) via signed USB image.
  2) Delta bundle + validation manifest for subsequent updates.
  3) Run sideload end-to-end test (install -> offline patch -> restart).
  Each phase has a short checklist and preflight.
Alex (AE): Good. What does the preflight look like? customer will run it with limited infra team.
Marta (SE): Preflight (short):
  - Check kernel deps + driver min versions
  - Verify available GPU/CPU footprint
  - Confirm root CA and offline signing key presence
  - Run `sha256sum bundle.tar.gz` and compare to manifest
  Example validation snippet we give them:
  ```
  # verify bundle signature
  sha256sum -c manifest.sha256
  openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
  ```
Jess (Ops): Ops notes: USB delivery OK but customer asked about chain-of-custody. We need signed SBOM and timestamped signatures. HSM-backed signing preferred; fallback to KMS-exportable key if HSM not available.
Charles (PM): Commercially, will this be treated as a standard POC or a sealed-deploy add-on? Need to flag potential cost uplift for custom bundling and engineering time.
Alex (AE): They filled out parts of the security questionnaire and asked: can we rotate certs offline during the POC? Also asked about upgrade cadence — they want quarterly security-only patches and optional major upgrades twice a year.
Marta (SE): Cert rotation offline: yes — our runbook supports offline CSR signing and root chain replacement. We include a short orchestration script for offline rotation. For cadence: we can commit to quarterly security deltas during the POC and document major upgrade windows.
Jess (Ops): Practical caveats:
  - Deltas must be small; recommend `rsync`-style diffs in minibundles to reduce USB size.
  - If they require hotpatching (no reboot), that increases risk and engineering time.
  - We need an ops contact on their side for validation and a test machine that mirrors prod.
Alex (AE): OK — can you draft the POC deliverables and the scoping note I can share with the customer? Include acceptance criteria.
Marta (SE): I'll drop a scoping note. Acceptance criteria draft:
  - Seed install successful on at least 1 host
  - Signed delta applied and verified (manifest + signature)
  - Offline cert rotation executed with validation
  - SBOM + signed provenance delivered
  - Runbook handed off to customer ops with one synchronous walkthrough
Charles (PM): Add a risk item: if they require third-party SCAP scans in-airgap that we haven't validated, include schedule impact (~3-5 days).
Alex (AE): Also they asked about pricing for signed bundles and 24/7 on-call during cutover. Any guidance?
Charles (PM): Standard: sealed POC packaging = one-time engineering prep fee + per-bundle signing/validation fee. 24/7 support is an enterprise add-on. I'll include ranges in the scoping doc rather than exact $s.
Marta (SE): For security questionnaire: attach these artifacts to the sales packet: `airgap-runbook.pdf`, `signed-sbom.zip`, `validation-manifest-example.json`, and `offline-rotation-script.sh`. Also include the sample commands above.
deploy-bot: New test bundle pushed to staging: `airgap-bundle-2024-11-05` (signed). CI notes: manifest + signature present.
Jess (Ops): One more ops note — if their environment blocks external time sources we need to ensure timestamping is included in signature metadata or use an internal TSA. Mention in runbook.
Alex (AE): Great. Timeline: Marta, can you put the scoping note + acceptance criteria in a short PDF by EOD? I'll share with GovCo tomorrow.
Marta (SE): Yes — I'll upload by 18:00 PT and add a checklist for the on-site engineer.
Alex (AE): Thanks everyone. I'll wait for the doc and then sync with legal on the SOW language for sealed delivery. :thumbsup:
